name: Sukh Sagar Restaurant
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor's #1 of 4 ranked Palitana restaurants — sits on Taleti Road, the staging area for the 4,000-step Shatrunjaya climb. Multi-cuisine and wheelchair-accessible (rare in Palitana), serving breakfast/lunch/dinner. The default pick for yatris who want a full sit-down meal rather than a dharmshala bhojanalay.
insider_tip: Open early for pre-climb breakfast (start the climb by 6 AM in summer to beat heat). Pure-veg only — Palitana town has a city-wide ban on meat sales, so there's no point asking elsewhere.

name: Hotel Sumeru (TCGL) Restaurant
why_it_matters: TCGL (Gujarat Tourism)-run 20-room property on Station Road, 500 metres from Palitana Railway Station — the safe-bet kitchen for first-time pilgrims arriving by train. Standardised pricing, government oversight on hygiene, and Jain-friendly menu options (no onion/garlic on request).
insider_tip: Government-run kitchens follow strict mealtime windows — lunch 12-2 PM, dinner 7-9 PM. Outside those hours, only tea is available. Ask for the 'satvik' or no-onion-garlic variant when booking dinner.
signature_address: Hotel Sumeru, Station Road, near Jakat Naka, near Gurukul High School, Palitana, Bhavnagar 364270

name: Siddhagiri Jain Bhojanshala
why_it_matters: Walking distance from the main Taleti market — the most-cited dedicated Jain bhojanshala by name in Palitana. Strict Jain protocol: no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato, beetroot), all meals served before sunset. The default for observant Jain yatris who want a hot home-style thali rather than a dharmshala mass meal.
insider_tip: Dinner is served before sunset per Jain dietary practice — finish by 6 PM in winter, 7 PM in summer. Cash only. No onion/garlic means the masala profile is gentler than standard Gujarati thali; ask for extra hari mirch if you want heat.
signature_address: Walking distance from main Taleti market, Palitana, Bhavnagar District 364270

name: Vijay Vilas Palace Dining Room
why_it_matters: Palitana's only proper heritage palace stay — commissioned 1906 by Yuvraj Vijay Sinhji of the Gohil dynasty, spread across 6 acres with 7 cottages. The lady of the house personally supervises a daily home-cooked Gujarati menu (sev tameta, dal, baingan, fresh-hot rotis); restaurant is part of the residential experience, not a walk-in commercial venue.
insider_tip: 4 km outside Palitana town — only worth it if you're staying, or if you book a meal as a non-resident in advance. Call ahead; the kitchen cooks to numbers, not a la carte. The garden lunch with the surrounding hill view is the signature setting.
signature_address: Village Adpur, PO Gheti, Palitana, Bhavnagar District 364270
